- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is negative or mixed (≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast gently, especially in early horizon.
- Model frequently overshoots after recent price spikes (e.g., +5–10% above true), especially if sentiment is neutral or positive — apply downward correction in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust — apply mean reversion correction toward prior 5–7 day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% prior 7-day avg + 30% sentiment-adjusted trend) to reduce volatility bias.
- If sentiment is high and price is rising, model often overpredicts; cap forecast at 1.2x recent 7-day high unless sentiment is strong and sustained.
- If sentiment is low and price is falling, model often underpredicts; add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast to avoid underestimating downside risk.
